parsed.explanation: State law is protective and codified, but the combined regime is governed at entry, in federal facilities and in federal custody by the national binary-sex regime. A document/presentation discrepancy can trigger refusal, extended screening and consideration of lifetime fraud ineligibility; federal facilities bar access congruent with identity; and documented federal custody included forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and sexual abuse. State non-discrimination, explicit hate-crime cover and working birth-certificate/licence processes mitigate street and state-service exposure, but do not cancel those federal interactions. Severity if outed is therefore major, with no credible execution pathway.

entry_documents.exposure: 2025 order and Feb 2025 cable: documents/records discrepancy or doubt about sex -> refusal and extra evidence; suspected wilful misrepresentation -> consider permanent fraud ineligibility. Trans-athlete entry ban. Reported passport confiscation/blocking for nationals abroad.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports valid to expiry; fraud requires four elements, limited waivers, never automatic; suit pending; several orders enjoined. State allows birth-certificate change without surgery and licence change by declaration.
entry_documents.interaction: Foreign visitor's home passport does not remove entry screening: discrepancy at border can move to refusal/fraud assessment and detention, regardless of state protections.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: From 2026 federal corrections model: short hair, hormone removal, psychiatric drugs described as conversion therapy; denial of care; stopped reporting trans prisoners. Immigration custody: forced labour, beatings, solitary, severe sexual abuse reported.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Not documented. State shortfalls on incarcerated trans protections noted without detail; no state custody protocol documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Entry/facilities discrepancy -> investigation -> immigration or criminal detention -> supermajority harm under federal custody rules; state anti-discrimination law does not govern federal custody.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with identity. State bans map: 9+1 units ban all government buildings, 9 ban schools plus some, 3 schools only; 4 criminalise in circumstances e.g. trespass after refusal to depart, with a 2025 capitol arrest and 24h men's-ward hold documented nationally.
federal_state_facilities.protection: This state is mapped Low-Risk, has codified gender-identity non-discrimination in public accommodations/services, and is not documented in a ban category. 29 units plus capital have no mapped ban.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: State buildings may be accessible, but federal buildings, installations and federally funded facilities in the same state remain under national ban; traveller cannot rely on state forum alone.

care_services.exposure: National EO calls minor gender care mutilation; proposed rules would bar public insurance under 18; DOJ subpoenaed 20+ hospitals for under-19 records. State rated short on healthcare equity without detail. Airport screening can out trans travellers.
care_services.protection: State conversion-therapy ban statewide since 2023, insurance-corporation non-discrimination; no state-specific care ban documented. Emergency care status not documented.
care_services.interaction: Adult routine care on visitor documents may proceed at state facilities, but federal funding/policy uncertainty and record exposure interact with entry/document checks.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National strategy prioritises groups described as radically pro-transgender; DOJ memo twice invokes radical gender ideology; funding freeze and forbidden-terms removal. Poll: 66% support birth-sex on documents, 69% birth-sex sports.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; state hate-crime law covers gender since 1992, explicit gender identity/expression added Jan 2025; gay/trans panic defence abolished July 2024.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State prosecution of bias crimes is a real remedy locally, but national enforcement framing, facility and entry directives operate despite it and signal institutional hostility.

minors_guardians.exposure: National orders target minor care, and direct investigation/prosecution of teachers facilitating social transition e.g. names/pronouns; women's sports EO and trans-athlete entry ban. Child care banned in 27 units nationally.
minors_guardians.protection: State conversion-therapy ban covers minors, non-discrimination codified, March 2025 sports resolution is advisory only and does not change law; school body cites conflict with state civil-rights act.
minors_guardians.interaction: Accompanying guardian/minor: entry as athlete, school enrolment, or seeking care can trigger federal scrutiny; state advisory-only sports measure does not create a state ban but federal entry rule remains.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No state-specific anti-trans violence or enforcement statistics documented. Nationally, bathroom arrest shows police will enforce facility rules; screening guides note invasive outing at checkpoints.
street_violence_police_response.protection: State non-discrimination codified 2023 after 2022 high-court ruling, explicit hate-crime cover, panic-defence abolition; 22 units plus capital outlaw gender-identity discrimination.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: State police/courts are documented as a recourse for bias/discrimination, but federal agents and facility enforcers are not bound by that state recourse.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Sodomy statute unrepealed but activity legal nationally since 2003, so tangential. Several national orders enjoined or in litigation; passport suit unresolved after Supreme Court allowed restrictions. Thin state-specific data on violence, custody detail, X licence marker.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Civil-liberties litigation, legal-aid FAQ, state commission from June 2023, state courts previously enforced protections.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies are split by sovereign: state remedies may work for state discrimination, federal remedies are slow/contested and do not block entry, facility or custody exposure in the moment.

anchor_checks.comparison: Higher/safer than 0.35-A: no routine visitor register, airline verification or discretionary expulsion without charge is documented; refusal is tied to discrepancy/fraud assessment, and state courts and codified protections provide real recourse for state matters.

Similar to 0.55-B: extended secondary screening for document mismatch, hours-long delay, possible refused admission and slow appeal. Here the fraud consequence can be lifetime ineligibility and federal custody abuse is documented, pulling slightly below, while state protections pull up.

Lower than 0.75-C: that anchor has brief detention, written reasons, counsel and compensation for unlawful holding with respectful border training. Here federal facilities are barred by policy, fraud ineligibility is expressly to be considered, and custody abuse is documented, so remedies do not reliably prevent exposure.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller encounters two interacting sovereigns. The state supplies operative protections - codified non-discrimination, explicit hate-crime cover, panic-defence abolition, conversion-therapy ban and document-change routes - which materially reduce street, housing and state-service risk. The national regime supplies the sharpest exposures - binary passport/entry rules with fraud consideration, federal facility exclusion, and severe documented federal custody practices - and state law does not pre-empt them. Minors face additional federal care/sports/school scrutiny, only partly buffered locally. Net: elevated risk, above routine-detention anchors but below jurisdictions where brief screening reliably ends in release and compensation.
